root_idea.summary: The root centers on tree leaves and foliage, with extensions to wealth or money through the abundance of leaves, and a distinct branch for ash-grey or dusky color.
root_idea.development: The leaf sense develops figurative associations with abundance, wealth, and silver; a separate color branch describes ash-grey hues and related terms for barren years and unsuccessful seeking.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested collective or plural foliage noun.
Distinct Quran-attested singulative noun meaning a single leaf.
Distinct Quran-attested noun for silver money, marked by a different vocalization.

senses.definition: Leaves or foliage of a tree.
senses.usage_conditions: Used as a collective or plural foliage term in the supplied Quranic occurrences.

senses.definition: A single leaf of a tree.
senses.usage_conditions: The singulative counterpart of وَرَق in the Quranic expression concerning any individual leaf.

senses.definition: Silver money or coined silver, including dirhams.
senses.usage_conditions: A money term distinguished by its vocalization from وَرَق meaning leaves.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wealth or abundant money, figuratively compared with the abundance of leaves.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative wealth sense distinct from وَرِق as coined silver.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The greenness of the ground produced by grass.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explicitly distinguished from the leaves of trees.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take or remove the leaves from a tree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive verbal use describing the stripping of a tree's foliage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Leafy; describing a tree with leaves, especially one with abundant foliage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally of trees or a tree's leafy covering.
A specialized plural usage of وَرَق distinct from the foliage sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hidden knot or protuberance within a branch.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun sense distinct from وَرَقَة meaning a leaf.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece or clot of blood; its plural is وَرَق.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is explained by comparison with fallen leaves.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weak men, figuratively likened to leaves in their weakness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural usage referring specifically to weak people.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fail to obtain what one seeks; of a hunter, to find that the prey has escaped or the hunt has failed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic extension from leaves covering a hunter's snare, also applied generally to an unsuccessful seeker.
The expression is associated with the ash-like appearance of a drought-stricken land.
A color noun, distinct from the foliage noun وَرَقَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dusky, ash-grey, or white tending toward black.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective used of a camel and, in the broader lexical evidence, of other beings having this hue.
A separate nominal use recorded for the same lexical form as the color adjective.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Silver and coined dirhams are covered by the Quranic silver sense.
The specialized plural sense meaning events is separately represented.
The ash-color noun sense is represented.
The leafy-tree adjective and abundant-foliage construction are represented.
The dusky or ash-grey color adjective is represented.
The separate noun sense 'ashes' is represented.

cautions: The foliage terms وَرَق and وَرَقَة are distinct from وَرِق, the silver-money term; classical evidence also records variant vocalizations for the silver word.
Several homonymous Classical Arabic branches—such as ash color, a hidden branch-knot, and a piece of blood—are kept separate from the Quranic foliage senses.
